summary: Major iteration 2 (PWA + JWT auth + 12 luxury services) tested end-to-end. Backend: 26/27 pytest pass (1 fail: brute-force lockout). Frontend: home + 12 services + QR card + login/register/portal flow + admin protection + availability calendar slot → booking-form prefill all working. PWA manifest + service worker reachable. Chat returns 503 gracefully (LLM budget).

critical.issue: Lockout key is `{request.client.host}:{email}`. Behind k8s ingress, requests round-robin between two proxy IPs (e.g. 10.208.130.77 and 10.208.130.78), so each IP only accumulates 2-3 fails out of 5 needed. Verified in mongo login_attempts: distinct identifier docs per proxy IP. A real attacker would never be rate-limited reliably from a single client. Fix: respect X-Forwarded-For (first IP), or key by email only, or by (X-Forwarded-For + email).

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout to use X-Forwarded-For (or email-only key) so it survives multi-proxy k8s ingress. Current implementation lets 10+ wrong logins through before any lock.

Optional: add `data-testid` attributes for availability-date / slot buttons / continue-to-booking / login fields. Tests had to fall back to text/role selectors. Not blocking but slows future regression.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py brute-force key uses `request.client.host` which is the immediate proxy IP, not the real client. Behind any load balancer this silently disables the protection.
POST /api/auth/refresh sets only access_token but does not rotate refresh_token — acceptable but worth documenting.
PATCH /api/bookings/{id} still takes status as query param; client-cancel logic looks correct but consider moving to a body-validated enum.
server.py uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown'); migrate to lifespan handlers.

Frontend AvailabilityCalendar + Booking communicate via sessionStorage + custom event (`cla:prefill`). Works, but a shared React context or query-string approach would be more testable and SEO-friendly.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (home, login, register, portal, admin protection, availability→booking prefill, sign-out, footer QR, PWA assets)

Re-run after main agent fixes brute-force. Frontend selectors used text-based fallbacks for slot buttons & continue — adding data-testid would help.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout failing in production: backend uses request.client.host as part of the identifier, but k8s ingress forwards requests through multiple proxy pods (verified IPs 10.208.130.77 / .78 in login_attempts collection). Each proxy IP accumulates its own count, so reaching the 5-fail threshold from a single browser/attacker takes 10+ attempts. Reproduction: 6 wrong logins from one session return 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401 instead of the expected …, 401, 429. Mitigation: read first IP from X-Forwarded-For header (FastAPI: request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip()) or drop the IP component and key by email only.
